h1:
Where to Stay in Hat Yai?
12 Hotels We Actually Reviewed
Prices Compared Across 3 Sites!
heroSub: 12 hand-picked Hat Yai hotels across every budget — a high-rise with a sky pool in the heart of the Lee Gardens shopping district, a 4-star linked straight into Central mall, a boutique in the Greenway area, and budget hotels and a hostel near the train station. From roughly ฿250–1,800/night.
introH2: 🏙️ Why does choosing the right area in Hat Yai matter so much?
introHtml: Hat Yai is a shopping-and-eating town packed into a small footprint — most people come to walk the markets, eat well and stock up on snacks to take home, so where you stay matters because the good stuff is all within walking distance. Stays fall into roughly four areas — the downtown Lee Gardens–Nipat Uthit district is the heart of Hat Yai, walkable to Kim Yong Market, Santisuk Market and the night market, ideal for walk-and-eat trips; the Greenway–Central Festival area is the big-mall and ASEAN Night Bazaar zone; near Hat Yai train station suits those arriving by rail or moving on; and the airport road (Kanchanawanit) suits self-drivers or early flights. Book without checking the area and you can end up calling cars back and forth all day. This guide rounds up 12 hand-picked Hat Yai hotels across every tier — all with real guest reviews, prices compared across 3 sites and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Hat Yai has no metro, but the centre is compact and the shopping districts are walkable; for longer hops a ride-hailing app or a songthaew is cheap and easy. Hat Yai Airport (HDY) is about a 25–30 minute drive from town. Pick by your itinerary: Lee Gardens–Nipat Uthit is downtown, walkable to Kim Yong Market, Santisuk Market and the night market, best for walk-and-eat trips; Greenway–Central Festival is the big-mall, ASEAN Night Bazaar and Central Festival zone, great for mall lovers; the train station area suits rail travellers and backpackers; and Kanchanawanit Road–airport side suits self-drivers or early flights. Almost every in-town hotel has parking — just ask when you book.

entries.name: Lee Gardens Plaza Hotel
entries.revCount: 476 reviews · 9.4, the highest in this guide · sky pool
entries.storyHtml: Lee Gardens Plaza is the highest-scoring hotel in this guide at 9.4 from 476 reviews. It's a 405-room high-rise right in the downtown Lee Gardens district; the standout is a sky pool with views over Hat Yai, and a location walkable to Kim Yong Market, Santisuk Market and the night market. Deluxe rooms start at ฿1,300, making it ideal for anyone who wants a central hotel with good rooms, great views and everything within walking distance.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: ask for a high-floor Deluxe City View for the full skyline, and head up to the sky pool at dusk when the city lights look their best.
pros: Highest score in the guide (9.4), good rooms and service
Sky pool with views over Hat Yai
Heart of Lee Gardens, walk to several markets
Beside the night market — eat and shop on foot
cons: A renovated older tower, some areas show their age
Lively downtown area; street-side rooms can hear the city

entries.name: Buri Sriphu Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Si Phuwanat Rd · Greenway · near ASEAN Night Bazaar
entries.addr: 310 Si Phuwanat Rd, Hat Yai, Songkhla
entries.storyHtml: Buri Sriphu is a 136-room 4-star boutique in the Greenway area scoring 9.0 from 426 reviews. Its standout is a saltwater pool — rare in Hat Yai — and a location near both the ASEAN Night Bazaar and Central Festival. Standard rooms start at ฿1,500, with a Honeymoon Suite for couples, making it a good pick for anyone who wants solid 4-star rooms in the mall-and-night-market zone without crowding into the very centre of town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: couples can look at the Honeymoon Suite, and if you like a swim, the saltwater pool feels easier on the eyes than the usual chlorine pool — best in the early evening.

Greenway area, quieter than the downtown core

entries.name: Centara Hotel Hat Yai

entries.storyHtml: Centara is the most-reviewed hotel in this guide, with 3,374 reviews and a score of 8.7. It's a 248-room 4-star that connects directly into Central mall from the building — you can shop without stepping outside — and it's walkable to Kim Yong Market. Superior rooms start at ฿1,800, with an Executive Suite that adds lounge access. With thousands of reviews backing a consistent standard, it suits families and anyone who wants a large central hotel with a mall built in.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: if the budget allows, step up to an Executive Suite for lounge access, and ask for a high floor for a more open city view.

entries.name: Crystal Hotel
entries.storyHtml: Crystal Hotel is a design hotel scoring 8.9 from 553 reviews. It's a 228-room property styled in warm, modern tones, with a sky pool and a Kanchanawanit Road location walkable to Central Festival and the CentralFest market. Deluxe Twins start at ฿1,200, and there's a Skyline Room with a jacuzzi for couples — a good pick for anyone who wants a stylish room in the Central Festival mall zone without a high price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: couples after something special can look at the Skyline Room with its jacuzzi; for a regular night, the Smart Deluxe King is a good-value, good-looking room.

entries.name: Hop Inn Hat Yai
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Kanchanawanit Rd · airport side of town
entries.storyHtml: Hop Inn Hat Yai is a standard budget-chain hotel scoring 8.6 from 340 reviews. The draw is clean, simple 19.6 sqm rooms to the same consistent standard as every branch, plus free parking. It sits on Kanchanawanit Road on the airport side of town, about 24–30 minutes' drive to Hat Yai Airport. Rooms start at ฿800 — ideal for self-drivers, early flights, or anyone who wants a clean, reliable room at a budget price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: a car is the easiest way here thanks to free parking and the airport-side location; without one, allow time to call a ride into the downtown markets.

faqTitle: FAQ — common traveller questions about Hat Yai hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area is best to stay in Hat Yai?
faq.a: It depends on your plans. Lee Gardens–Nipat Uthit (downtown) is walkable to Kim Yong Market, Santisuk Market and the night market, best for walk-and-eat trips (Lee Gardens Plaza, Asian Hotel, Lee Gardens Hotel, B2 Rat Uthit). Greenway–Central Festival is the big-mall and ASEAN Night Bazaar zone (Buri Sriphu, Crystal, Centara). Near the train station suits rail travellers (The Bedroom, Hatyai Backpackers). Kanchanawanit Road–airport side suits self-drivers or early flights (Hop Inn).

faq.q: ❓ How much do Hat Yai hotels cost?
faq.a: Hat Yai is very affordable: hostel dorm beds start around ฿250 (Hatyai Backpackers); budget hotels and boutiques (3-star) run about ฿450–900 (The Bedroom, B2 Rat Uthit, Ido, Asian, Lee Gardens Hotel, BP Grand Tower, Hop Inn); and central 4-star hotels run about ฿1,200–1,800 (Crystal, Lee Gardens Plaza, Buri Sriphu, Centara).

faq.q: ❓ Where should I stay to shop Kim Yong and Santisuk markets?
faq.a: Kim Yong Market and Santisuk Market are downtown in the Nipat Uthit–Lee Gardens area. Walkable stays include Lee Gardens Plaza (high-rise by the night market, ฿1,300), Asian Hotel (Nipat Uthit 3, ฿700), B2 Rat Uthit (฿670) and Lee Gardens Hotel (in the Lee Garden building, ฿900) — ideal for walk-and-eat trips with no cars needed.

faq.q: ❓ Which Hat Yai hotels have a swimming pool?
faq.a: In this guide the ones with a pool are Lee Gardens Plaza (sky pool with city views, ฿1,300), Buri Sriphu (saltwater pool, ฿1,500) and Crystal Hotel (sky pool, ฿1,200) — all central 4-star hotels with a pool at a reasonable price.

faq.q: ❓ Arriving by train — which hotels are near Hat Yai station?
faq.a: Stays walkable to Hat Yai train station are The Bedroom (฿450, a small canalside boutique by the station) and Hatyai Backpackers Hostel (฿250, a 9-minute walk from the station), both ideal for rail travellers or onward journeys. For self-drivers or early flights, Hop Inn Hat Yai sits on the airport side with free parking.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Hat Yai hotel?
faq.a: On ordinary weekdays, 1–2 weeks ahead is enough. But Hat Yai is a shopping town very popular with Malaysian and Singaporean visitors, so good central rooms fill fast on long weekends, holidays and weekends — book 2–4 weeks ahead or more, especially for the 4-star hotels around Lee Gardens.
